messages:
Anna: Heads-up — saw a reproducible spike in pass-through latency and a handful of NaNs on the paged-attn path for a few customer traces. Seems tied to large sequence prefixes + fp8 quantized KV. Posting microbench logs and a quick hypothesis.

Anna: Repro steps: run `bench/paged_attn_profile --seq 4096 --batch 8 --kv-quant=fp8` on r23 branch. After ~1200 steps we see a jump in time per token and occasional `inf` in the softmax exponent stats.

Anna: Minimal log snippet:```
[perf] step 1189 token_time: 13.7ms -> 27.4ms
[stat] exp_max: 1.2e+38 exp_inf_count: 3
[stat] kvcache_slots_used: 4096 alignment: 128
```

Jamal: :eyes: do we have the exact kernel variant that ran? flash-variant or fused fallback?

Anna: It flips to the paged-fallback kernel (kernel_id: page_v2_delayed) when prefix length > 2048 and alignment crosses 64->128 boundary. The kernel selector metric shows a hysteresis change at 2048 seq.

Priya: Could be a rescale/denorm issue in the fp8 path. If scaling factor computed from max logits is clipped incorrectly, exp() gets huge. Any checks in the fp8 quant decode path?

Ciara: I inspected the quant decode: we dequantize K/V then apply an inplace `scale *= 2.0f` adjustment for historical reasons (back-compat rescale). That double-rescale might be wrong for paged KV where we store/resume prefixes.

Mike: Also the KV alignment change can change memory layout which affects vectorized exp implementations (we call a fast SIMD exp that assumes contiguous lanes). If lane stride != expected, some inputs blow up.

Anna: Agreed. Hypothesis: (a) misapplied historical rescale on resumed KV blocks, (b) kernel switch causes different exp implementation with different numeric stability, (c) fp8 range pushes intermediate logits near the overflow threshold.

Priya: Quick patch idea: add a guarded clamp before exp with a diagnostic flag, and disable the historical rescale for resumed blocks. Patch diff:```diff
- kv_block.scale *= 2.0f;
+ if (!kv_block.resumed) kv_block.scale *= 2.0f;
+ // diagnostic clamp
+ logits = std::min(logits, 88.0f); // ~log(max_float)
```

Jamal: Add a perf flag to avoid always clamping in prod. For the experiment set `RUNTIME_NUMERIC_GUARD=1` to collect counts. perf-bot can aggregate.

perf-bot: Collected numeric-guard metrics for run r23-2026-03-17: exp_clamp_triggers=12, exp_inf=0, token_time_median=14.0ms

Ciara: Nice — clamp removed the `inf`s and reduced spike frequency. But median token time increased by ~0.3ms due to extra branch. We need a lower-cost long-term fix.

Mike: Next steps: 1) remove historical rescale on resumed KV 2) add a fast-vector-safe exp fallback that handles non-unit strides 3) tune kernel selector hysteresis so we don't flip at 2048 for this model family.

Priya: I can work on (1). Quick unit test plan: create a resumed KV scenario with fp8 random seeds and assert no inf/NaN across 10k tokens and compare output L2 to fp16 baseline < 1e-3.

Anna: I'll own (2) + selector tuning. Can we also run the sampling benchmark with representative traffic (long prefixes + mixed batch sizes) to make sure batching heuristics don't force the kernel switchover? I suspect our batch-sampler pushes some traces into the 2048+ bucket.

Jamal: I'll queue a canary job: `canary/multi-model-longprefix-1000` with both r22 (baseline) and r23 (w/guard) and collect token-tail percentiles.

perf-bot: Canary queued: id=cb-3391. Will post results in ~2h.

Ciara: Also, log a follow-up to docs: we need to record that rescale semantics differ for resumed vs cold KV to avoid future regressions.

Anna: Summary: temporary numeric guard mitigates infs, confirmed rescale bug on resumed KV, perf hit small but acceptable for canary. Attaching mini-profiling snippet (timings in ms):```
variant    p50   p90   p99
page_v1    12.8  16.1  23.0
page_v2    13.1  27.4  78.2  <-- spikes due to exp overflow events
fused_attn 11.9  15.0  19.7
```

Mike: Good. If the fused_attn variant avoids the path we might prefer routing long-prefix traffic to it until we have the vector fix. Add routing override as short-term mitigation.

Anna: Will do. Anyone object to landing Priya's resumed-rescale patch behind a feature flag and the diagnostic guard in master? Plan: land both, run canary, then iterate.

Jamal: :thumbsup:

Ciara: :+1:

Mike: go for it.

Anna: I'll open PRs and link here. PRs: #4128 (rescale fix, feature-flag), #4129 (numeric-guard, diagnostic).
